record.paper_title: Optimal scaling of average queue sizes in an input-queued switch: an open problem
record.original_question: For an n by n input-queued switch operating in discrete time, with n input ports and n output ports, each feasible schedule a matching between input and output ports, independent Bernoulli arrivals with rates λ_i,j, load factor ρ(λ) defined as the maximum over all input-row and output-column aggregate arrival rates, and Q*(n,λ) the minimum over all scheduling policies of the steady-state expected total queue size E[sum_i,j Q_i,j], what is β*_0, the infimum over positive exponents β for which there is a constant c > 0 such that Q*(n,λ) is at most c n^β divided by 1 − ρ(λ), uniformly for all n and all arrival-rate matrices λ with 0 < ρ(λ) < 1? In particular, is β*_0 equal to 1?

evidence.quote: Find β∗0, the infimum over all positive numbers β for which there exists a constant c > 0 such that Q∗(n,λ) ≤ c · nβ/(1 − ρ(λ)).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an $n \times n$ input-queued switch operating in discrete time. There are $n$ input ports and $n$ output ports, and a separate queue $Q_{i,j}$ for each input-output pair $(i,j)$, $1 \le i,j \le n$. At each time step:

(i) Arrivals: for each $(i,j)$, a packet arrives at queue $(i,j)$ independently with probability $\lambda_{i,j} \in [0,1)$, where $\lambda = (\lambda_{i,j})$ is a fixed matrix of arrival rates.

(ii) Service: a scheduler selects a matching $\sigma$ between input and output ports (i.e., a permutation, or partial matching, of $\{1,\dots,n\}$); for each pair $(i,\sigma(i))$ in the matching with $Q_{i,\sigma(i)}>0$, one packet departs from queue $(i,\sigma(i))$.

Define the load factor
$$\rho(\lambda) \;=\; \max\!\left\{\max_{1\le i\le n}\sum_{j=1}^n \lambda_{i,j},\;\; \max_{1\le j\le n}\sum_{i=1}^n \lambda_{i,j}\right\}.$$
Assume $0<\rho(\lambda)<1$, so the system is stabilizable. Let $Q^*(n,\lambda)$ denote the infimum, over all (possibly history-dependent) scheduling policies that render the queue-length Markov chain positive recurrent, of the steady-state expectation $\mathbb{E}\!\left[\sum_{i,j} Q_{i,j}\right]$.

Define
$$\beta^*_0 \;=\; \inf\Big\{\beta>0:\ \exists\, c>0\ \text{such that}\ Q^*(n,\lambda)\le \frac{c\, n^{\beta}}{1-\rho(\lambda)}\ \text{for all }n\ge 1\ \text{and all }\lambda\ \text{with}\ 0<\rho(\lambda)<1\Big\}.$$

Determine $\beta^*_0$. In particular, decide whether $\beta^*_0=1$.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture $\beta^*_0=1$ remains open in general. Partial progress includes a result establishing the optimal $\Theta(n/(1-\rho))$ scaling in the heavy-traffic regime $1-\rho = O(1/n^2)$ (Shah–Tsitsiklis–Zhong, 2014), and subsequent improvements via graph factorization yielding bounds like $O(n(1-\rho)^{-4/3}\log(\cdot))$ for uniform arrivals (2019) and $O(n^{5/4}/(1-\rho))$ in certain regimes (2022). No full resolution showing $\beta^*_0=1$ uniformly over all $n$ and $\lambda$ has been published as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Optimal queue-size scaling in switched networks
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes optimal scaling in the heavy-traffic regime 1-rho = O(1/n^2), confirming the conjecture in that regime only.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture resolved only in a special regime, not in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Improved queue-size scaling for input-queued switches via graph factorization
status_evidence.snippet: Scheduling policies achieving O(n(1-rho)^{-4/3} log(...)) for uniform arrivals.
status_evidence.claim: Partial improvements toward conjectured O(n/(1-rho)) scaling.

status_evidence.title: An algorithm for improved delay-scaling in input-queued switches
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithm with expected total queue length O(n^{5/4}(1-rho)^{-1} log) in certain regimes.
status_evidence.claim: Further partial progress; full conjecture still unresolved.
